sections.h2: Who handles property tax in La Paz County, Arizona?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The La Paz County Assessor values property and keeps ownership, parcel maps, exemptions, mobile homes and business personal property. The La Paz County Treasurer mails the bills and collects the money. The Assessor does not set tax rates, issue bills, or collect or refund taxes, so a question about an amount due goes to the Treasurer and a question about value goes to the Assessor.

  • Treasurer: 1112 Joshua Avenue, Suite 203, Parker, AZ 85344. Open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., closed Fridays.
  • Assessor: 1112 Joshua Avenue, Suite 204, Parker, AZ 85344, phone 928-669-6165.
  • Recorder: records deeds and answers fee questions at 928-669-6136.

The Assessor gets deed information from the Recorder and permit information from La Paz County Community Development, the Town of Parker and the Town of Quartzsite. A house that gains a room or loses a roof without a permit can still show up on the roll later, so keep your permit paperwork in the sale file.

sections.h2: What kind of county is La Paz County for a home seller?
sections.html:
La Paz County is a large, thinly settled county on Arizona's western edge with a small tax base. It covers 4,514 square miles, had 16,557 residents in the 2020 census, and its seat is Parker, the largest town. Quartzsite is the only other incorporated town. The Colorado River Indian Reservation lies in the western part of the county.

Voters created La Paz County in 1983 by separating the northern part of Yuma County, and it is the only Arizona county formed after statehood. Census figures show 13,457 housing units in 2020, of which 45.2% were vacant, and 71.8% of occupied homes were owner-occupied. Mobile homes are part of the local housing stock, and the Assessor's office keeps mobile home records.

The Assessor's FAQ explains one local wrinkle. The office updates mobile home ownership from Motor Vehicle Division title records, and it cannot change the owner on the roll until the new title is issued. If the old owner is still on the title, the old owner still gets the notice of value and the tax bill. Before you sell a mobile home, confirm the title has moved.

sections.h2: When are La Paz County property taxes due in 2026 and 2027?
sections.html:
Half of the tax is due on October 1 and the other half on the following March 1, under A.R.S. 42-18052. The Treasurer's notice for the 2026 roll gives these dates and a 6:00 p.m. delinquency hour.

DateWhat happens
October 1, 2026First half due. Bills were mailed September 11.
November 2, 2026, 6:00 p.m.First half delinquent. This date has passed.
December 31, 2026Last day to pay the full year and avoid interest.
March 1, 2027Second half due.
May 4, 2027, 6:00 p.m.Second half delinquent.

Source: La Paz County Treasurer. Postmarked payments are accepted, and the smallest accepted payment is $10 or 10% of the tax due, whichever is greater.

If you owe the first half and have not paid it, interest is already running. Paying the whole year by December 31 stops further interest under A.R.S. 42-18053, so a seller who closes in December can clear it at the table.

sections.h2: How much interest does La Paz County charge on late tax?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes bear interest at 16% a year, simple, from the delinquency date, and a fraction of a month counts as a whole month. That rate comes from A.R.S. 42-18053. The Treasurer states the same 16%, prorated monthly from the first day of the month until paid.

  • No interest is collected if the delinquency came from an error by the assessor or treasurer.
  • No interest is collected if the full-year tax is paid on or before December 31 of the tax year.
  • The treasurer may waive interest and penalties once per property for a delinquency in the year after a mortgage or deed of trust is released, if the board of supervisors approves.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure good through your expected closing date. Parcel lookup and card payments run through the Treasurer's website. Card payments carry a convenience fee of $4.00 on a Visa debit card or 2.55% on a credit card, and the jurisdiction code to give by phone is 1312.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a La Paz County valuation?
sections.html:
File a petition with the County Assessor within 60 days after the Assessor mailed your notice of value. That deadline is in A.R.S. 42-16051, and a postmark counts as the filing date. Notices go out each year to the owner of record, and the county tells owners that only the full cash value or the property class can be appealed.

The petition has to state your opinion of full cash value and give substantial information backing it. The statute names three methods: the income approach, the market approach (with at least one comparable property or the sale of the subject property), and the cost approach. A recent arm's-length sale of your own house is the strongest comparable you can offer.

The limited property value is separate. The Assessor's notice page explains that Proposition 117 caps growth in limited property value at 5% a year, with exceptions listed in A.R.S. Title 42, Chapter 13, Article 7. Because bills run on limited value, a jump in full cash value does not always raise your tax by the same amount.

sections.h2: What tax relief exists for La Paz County homeowners?
sections.html:
The Assessor's FAQ describes two programs, and the office can give you the current income and value limits. Call 928-669-6165 before you list.

  • Exemption for widows, widowers and totally disabled persons age 17 or over. You must live in Arizona, meet income requirements, and stay under an indexed assessed-value limit. A disability claim needs a physician's certification that the disability is total and permanent.
  • Senior Property Valuation Protection, often called the senior freeze. It freezes limited property value for three years. You must be 65 at the time of application, use the home as your primary Arizona residence, and meet income rules.

The FAQ adds that a value can jump when a buyer takes over a home whose prior owner held a senior freeze. A buyer should expect a first notice of value that looks higher than the seller's. The Assessor's page also lists a rental registration form and points rental owners to the state's online lodging marketplace registration for short-term rentals.

sections.h2: How does unpaid tax affect a sale in La Paz County?
sections.html:
Property tax is a lien on the house, and under A.R.S. 42-17153 it attaches on January 1 of the tax year. It outranks other liens except those held by the state and tax liens from other years. It stays until the taxes, penalties, charges and interest are paid, a tax sale vests title in a buyer, or a certificate of removal and abatement is issued. A buyer's title company will therefore expect that the current year and any back years are paid from your proceeds.

The deed itself has a few requirements. A deed that transfers title must carry a sworn affidavit of property value from seller and buyer under A.R.S. 11-1133, and the recorder must refuse a deed without it unless it carries an exemption notation. The La Paz County Recorder lists the document rules online: paper 8 1/2 inches wide and 11 to 14 inches long, a two-inch top margin on the first page, original ink signatures, and the right fee. Ask the Recorder's office for the current fee schedule at 928-669-6136.

Selling a house with tax due is routine when the numbers are clear. Get the payoff from the Treasurer, confirm the owner of record with the Assessor, and give both numbers to the title company.

faqs.q: Are La Paz County property taxes still open to pay in November 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The first half became delinquent on November 2, 2026 at 6:00 p.m., so interest of 16% a year is accruing on that half. Paying the full year on or before December 31, 2026 stops interest from running under A.R.S. 42-18053. The second half is due March 1, 2027 and is delinquent after May 4, 2027.

faqs.q: Where do I pay La Paz County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the County Treasurer at 1112 Joshua Avenue, Suite 203, Parker, Arizona 85344, by mail or in person, or pay online or by phone. The office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and closed Fridays. Card payments add a $4.00 fee on Visa debit or 2.55% on credit cards.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my La Paz County notice of value?
faqs.a: You have 60 days from the date the Assessor mailed the notice. File a petition with the County Assessor stating your opinion of full cash value and the information that supports it. A.R.S. 42-16051 accepts the postmark as the filing date.

faqs.q: Does La Paz County have a senior property tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor administers Senior Property Valuation Protection, which freezes limited property value for three years. The owner must be 65 at application, live in the home as a primary Arizona residence, and meet income limits. Call the Assessor at 928-669-6165 for the form and current limits.

faqs.q: Can I sell a La Paz County house that still has tax due?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien attaches on January 1 of the tax year and is paid from sale proceeds at closing. Get a payoff amount from the Treasurer for your closing date, since interest runs monthly on delinquent amounts, and give it to the title company.
